DistiLLM avoids both the divergence selection problem and the variance problem by engineering a mixture target that is numerically stable by construction, but at the cost of adding a replay buffer (mixing on-policy and off-policy data) and an adaptive scheduler that adds hyperparameter complexity. The progression from GKD through MiniLLM to DistiLLM thus traces a shift from algorithmic simplicity toward computational and engineering sophistication, with later methods often addressing specific limitations of earlier approaches.
